arxiv-1704-05246.title: PhD Thesis
arxiv-1704-05246.creator: \ttitle
arxiv-1704-05246.description: Abstract The thesis focuses on the prediction of solvation thermodynamics using integral equation theories. Our main goal is to improve the approach using a rational correction. We achieve it by extending recently introduced pressure correction, and rationalizing it in the context of solvation entropy. The improved model (to which we refer as advanced pressure correction) is rather universal.

arxiv-2002-04498.title: Reaching, Grasping and Re-grasping: Learning Multimode Grasping Skills
arxiv-2002-04498.creator: Wenbin Hu, Chuanyu Yang, Kai Yuan, Zhibin Li
arxiv-2002-04498.description: Abstract The ability to adapt to uncertainties, recover from failures, and coordinate between hand and fingers are essential sensorimotor skills for fully autonomous robotic grasping. In this paper, we aim to study a unified feedback control policy for generating the finger actions and the motion of hand to accomplish seamlessly coordinated tasks of reaching, grasping and re-grasping.

arxiv-2103-05211.title: Combing a double helix
arxiv-2103-05211.creator: Thomas Bolton Plumb-Reyes, Nicholas Charles, L. Mahadevan
arxiv-2103-05211.description: Abstract Combing hair involves brushing away the topological tangles in a collective curl. Using a combination of experiment and computation, we study this problem that naturally links topology, geometry and mechanics. Observations show that the dominant interactions in hair are those of a two-body nature, corresponding to a braided homochiral double helix.

arxiv-2110-09422.title: The number and location of Jupiter’s circumpolar cyclones explained by vorticity dynamics
arxiv-2110-09422.creator: Nimrod Gavriel, Yohai Kaspi
arxiv-2110-09422.description: Abstract The Juno mission observed that both poles of Jupiter have polar cyclones that are surrounded by a ring of circumpolar cyclones. The North Pole holds eight circumpolar cyclones and the South Pole possesses five, with both circumpolar rings positioned along latitude ∼ 84 ∘ \sim 84^{\circ} N/S.

arxiv-2402-06290.title: On the Feasibility of Battery-Less LoRaWAN Communications using Energy Harvesting
arxiv-2402-06290.creator: Carmen Delgado 1 , José María Sanz 2 , Jeroen Famaey 1
arxiv-2402-06290.description: Abstract From the outset, batteries have been the main power source for the Internet of Things (IoT). However, replacing and disposing of billions of dead batteries per year is costly in terms of maintenance and ecologically irresponsible. Since batteries are one of the greatest threats to a sustainable IoT, battery-less devices are the solution to this problem.

arxiv-2402-15311.title: Scaling Limit of the Kuramoto Model on Random Geometric Graphs
arxiv-2402-15311.creator: Francisco Cirelli, Pablo Groisman, Ruojun Huang, Hernán Vivas
arxiv-2402-15311.description: Abstract . We consider the Kuramoto model on a graph with nodes given by n n i.i.d. points uniformly distributed on the d d dimensional torus. Two nodes are declared neighbors if they are at distance less than ϵ \epsilon .

arxiv-2410-02880.title: Bayesian Inference of Multiple Ising Models for Heterogeneous Public Opinion Survey Networks
arxiv-2410-02880.creator: Alejandra Avalos-Pacheco, Andrea Lazzerini, Monia Lupparelli, Francesco C. Stingo
arxiv-2410-02880.description: Abstract In public opinion studies, the relationships between opinions on different topics are likely to shift based on the characteristics of the respondents. Thus, understanding the complexities of public opinion requires methods that can account for the heterogeneity in responses across different groups.

arxiv-2411-01592.title: Decidability Issues for Petri Nets -- a survey 1 1 1 A former version of this paper appeared in the Concurrency Column of the EATCS Bulletin 52. Javier Esparza ∗ Mogens Nielsen Institut für Informatik BRICS ∗∗ Technische Universität München Computer Science Department Arcisstr. 21 Aarhus University
arxiv-2411-01592.description: Abstract We survey 25 years of research on decidability issues for Petri nets. We collect results on the decidability of important properties, equivalence notions, and temporal logics. 1 Introduction Petri nets are one of the most popular formal models for the representation and analysis of parallel processes. They are due to C.A.

arxiv-2412-08808.title: Wave Function Renormalization in Asymptotically Safe Quantum Gravity
arxiv-2412-08808.creator: Hikaru Kawai
arxiv-2412-08808.description: Abstract We discuss the effect of wave function renormalization (WFR) in asymptotically safe gravity. We show that there are two WFR-invariant quantities, and the renormalization (RG) equations may be written entirely in terms of these quantities. The same set of RG equations can be obtained whether we fix the vacuum energy or Newton coupling along the RG trajectory.

arxiv-2602-10013.title: Learning Force-Regulated Manipulation with a Low-Cost Tactile-Force-Controlled Gripper
arxiv-2602-10013.creator: Xuhui Kang, Tongxuan Tian, Sung-Wook Lee, Binghao Huang, Yunzhu Li, Yen-Ling Kuo
arxiv-2602-10013.description: Abstract Successfully manipulating many everyday objects, such as potato chips, requires precise force regulation. Failure to modulate force can lead to task failure or irreversible damage to the objects. Humans can precisely achieve this by adapting force from tactile feedback, even within a short period of physical contact. We aim to give robots this capability.

britannica-1911-weber-s-law.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-weber-s-law.description: Article 'Weber's Law' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. first enunciated by the German scientist, Ernst Heinrich Weber (1795-1878), who became professor at Leipzig (of anatomy, 1818, of physiology, 1840). He was specially famous for his researches into aural and cutaneous sensations.

plos-pone-0012037.creator: Aurelia Santoro, Valentina Balbi, Elisa Balducci et al.
plos-pone-0012037.description: PLOS ONE research article. Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disease and the leading cause of dementia among senile subjects. It has been proposed that AD can be caused by defects in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. Given the fundamental contribution of the mitochondrial

pmc-10808809.title: The effects of lower limb ischaemic preconditioning: a systematic review
pmc-10808809.creator: Chloe French, Dan Robbins, Marie Gernigon, Dan Gordon
pmc-10808809.description: Ischaemic preconditioning (IPC) involves the use of repeated occlusions and reperfusions of the peripheral muscle blood supply at a limb. This systematic literature review examines the typical responses in response to the method of application during an IPC applied at the lower limb.

pmc-11658418.title: Epigenome-wide association studies identify novel DNA methylation sites associated with PTSD: a meta-analysis of 23 military and civilian cohorts
pmc-11658418.creator: Seyma Katrinli, Agaz H. Wani, Adam X. Maihofer, Andrew Ratanatharathorn, Nikolaos P. Daskalakis, Janitza Montalvo-Ortiz, Diana L. Núñez-Ríos, Anthony S. Zannas, Xiang Zhao, Allison E. Aiello, Allison E. Ashley-Koch, Diana Avetyan, Dewleen G. Baker, Jean C. Beckham, Marco P. Boks, Leslie A. Brick, Ev
pmc-11658418.description: BackgroundThe occurrence of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following a traumatic event is associated with biological differences that can represent the susceptibility to PTSD, the impact of trauma, or the sequelae of PTSD itself. These effects include differences in DNA methylation (DNAm), an important form of epigenetic gene regulation, at multiple CpG loci across the genome.

pmc-13091031.title: Long-term recurrence-free survival following total penectomy and additional chemotherapy for solitary penile metastasis from muscle invasive bladder cancer
pmc-13091031.creator: Daiki Ishikawa, Taku Naiki, Aya Naiki-Ito, Hiroko Suzuki, Yohei Tsubouchi, Nobuhiko Shimizu, Toshiharu Morikawa, Maria Aoki, Masakazu Gonda, Noriyasu Kawai, Yukihiro Umemoto, Takahiro Yasui
pmc-13091031.description: Penile metastasis from bladder cancer is extremely rare and often presents as part of multiple distant metastases. However, no established standard treatment exists for a solitary penile metastasis. We report an 83-year-old male diagnosed with a solitary penile metastasis two years after radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

pmc-13279329.title: Fecal microbiota and microbial community transplantation: a review of current research
pmc-13279329.creator: Vitaly Ryazanov, Irina Vershinina, Ksenia Inchagova, Elena Bukareva, Vladimir Kolpakov, Alexey Ruchay, Dianna Kosyan, Maxim Marinchev, Alexey Zdorov
pmc-13279329.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Homeostasis across diverse ecosystems, ranging from human hosts to environmental matrices, is profoundly governed by microbial communities. Dysbiosis, the disruption of this microbial equilibrium, leads to significant adverse outcomes in medicine, agriculture, aquaculture, and environmental health. This review synthesizes current knowledge on microbial transfusions, defined as the deliberate transfer of microbial communities or their components to restore, reconstitute, or enhance functional capacities across these systems.

pmc-13321868.title: Geographic and population disparities in cutaneous melanoma in the United States: state-level trends and national population-level analyses
pmc-13321868.creator: Biaoyou Chen, Yijing Tang, Jiajia Lin, Xian Wei, Zihao Wang, Han Wang, Duoping Wang
pmc-13321868.description: BackgroundOver recent decades, cutaneous melanoma (CM) incidence in the United States (US) has increased but now appears to be plateauing, whereas mortality has declined. However, much less is known about how CM incidence and mortality vary between states, or about how differences between states in incidence relate to lifestyle factors, ambient UV exposure, and prevention or health care resources.

pmc-13550574.title: Sequencing approaches in hereditary cancer testing: strengths, limitations and future directions
pmc-13550574.creator: Sami Belhadj, Christopher J. Hatch, Holly LaDuca, Carolyn Horton, Seth I. Berger, Rachid Karam
pmc-13550574.description: Over the past three decades, Hereditary Cancer Testing (HCT) has evolved from single gene assays into multigene panel testing (MGPT), which allows for the screening of all known hereditary cancer genes in a single assay. MGPT is currently the standard approach for clinical HCT.

pmc-13569567.title: Diagnosing Barriers to California Bay-Delta Wetland Restoration Implementation: Extending the Adaptation Perspective
pmc-13569567.creator: Kyra Gmoser-Daskalakis, Mark Lubell, Gwen Arnold
pmc-13569567.description: Climate adaptation increasingly considers wetland restoration as a nature-based solution to reduce flood risk and provide co-benefits such as species protection, water resource management, and public recreation access. However, barriers must be identified and overcome to increase the pace and scale of wetland restoration for adaptive benefits.

pmc-13674511.title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
pmc-13674511.creator: Ran Huo, Shengyun Huang, Dixiang Gong, Xin Zhou, Heng Zhu, Pengyun Zhang, Hideaki Okuyama, Guangyu Bao, Xuan Li, Aram Bahmani, Lisa Martignetti, Zixin Zhang, Hongyu Hou, Changhong Cao, Yixun Cheng, Wei Gao, Dongling Ma, Nicole Y. K. Li-Jessen, Jianyu Li
pmc-13674511.description: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior.

pmc-13679022.title: Preoperative platelet-related inflammatory burden is associated with delayed early hemodynamic recovery following minimally invasive cardiac surgery
pmc-13679022.creator: Bekir Boğachan Akkaya, Enis Burak Gül, Gizem Işık, Abdülkadir Yılmaz, Mustafa Akdi, Sinan Sabit Kocabeyoğlu, Hayrettin Levent Mavioğlu
pmc-13679022.description: BackgroundMinimally invasive cardiac surgery (MICS) is associated with reduced surgical trauma and improved postoperative recovery; however, early hemodynamic recovery remains variable and may be influenced by patient-related biological factors. This study evaluated the association between preoperative inflammatory biomarkers and delayed early postoperative recovery following MICS.
